PURPOSE. Screen two candidate fixes for the hidden-bench prose problems against a fresh baseline, with the SAME harness for all arms. Arms:
- `base`: the current story package at /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/data/stories/continuity-initiative (working tree).
- `B`: a temporary copy of that package whose plot.md bench Details line is changed. The exact old line in plot.md is `**Details:** ordinary park bench; damaged grounds; service path; checkpoints; emergency patrols` and the exact new line is `**Details:** The park bench is fixed in place.; damaged grounds; service path; checkpoints; emergency patrols`. Replace only that one line; the harness must fail loudly if the old line is not found exactly once.
- `C`: the base package, but its captured find-state request (system and user text) has exactly one line removed on this diagnostic arm only: `- Brandon Corfman may say this aloud: I won't tell you that. Keep your voice down; patrols are nearby.` Do the removal on the captured payload text by exact whole-line match, fail loudly unless exactly one such line exists, and do not remove or alter anything else (the CHARACTERS biography stays). This is a recorded-prompt diagnostic, not a package edit.
States: `opening`, `inspect` (command `Inspect the park bench.`) and `find` (command `Look under the park bench.`), each captured through the same world-aware, hermetically stubbed provider path as the prose probe (scene 1B state, Kristin on the park bench). Arm C only exists for the `inspect` and `find` states.

MODES (argparse, mutually exclusive, like the prose probe):
1. `--capture --out FILE.json`: write all arm payloads (ids like `base-find`, `B-find`, `C-find`) with system, user and composed_segments.
2. `--validate`: the free structural checks, exit non-zero with a message on any failure: (a) the package files of arm B differ from base in exactly one line of plot.md and nowhere else (compare every file in the two package directories); (b) for arms base and B, in the opening and inspect payloads the three hidden bench clue names (`Transit token`, `handwritten number sequence`, `Michelle's photograph`, matched case-insensitively as plain substrings) do not appear anywhere in system or user text; (c) the find payload of every arm still contains the exact delivery sentence `Kristin reaches beneath the park bench. She retrieves a transit token, a handwritten number sequence and Michelle's photograph. She keeps all three with her.` in its request text and in composed_segments; (d) arm B's find payload differs from base's find payload and the text of the new Details sentence `The park bench is fixed in place.` appears in B's payload but not in base's; (e) arm C's find and inspect payloads equal base's with exactly that one line removed (compute by line operations, not by diffing prose).
3. `--dry-run`: print planned calls (find-state only: arms base, B, C x 10 samples = 30), token estimate and USD ceiling using the prose probe's cost constants, and refuse with a non-zero exit when over `--max-calls` (default 30) or `--max-usd` (default 0.03).
4. `--run --confirm --out ROWS.json`: the billed mode, structured exactly like the prose probe's `run_rows`: refuses unless CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_URL and CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_TOKEN are set (read from env, never print them), refuses if the output file already exists (once only, no replacement samples), writes rows incrementally with a `stop_reason`, stops on 429/401/403/5xx without replacing a sample, never retries. Each row: call_index, payload_id, arm, state, sample, response_text, plus the SAME provider-built `composed_segments` for that payload.
5. `--sheets --rows ROWS.json --out DIR`: blind sheets for human labelling. Shuffle with a fixed seed, opaque ids `sample-NNN`, a blind_key.json, a labels_template.json with the label names below set to null, and a `labels.freeze.json` hash written by the same method as the prose probe. Each sheet section shows `State:`, `Sample:`, then the model reply under `Narrator:` and the appended segment(s) under `Engine (appended by the game):`, never the arm or payload id. A bijection test (key row_index set is exactly 1..N, entries match the rows) must be in your tests.
6. `--report --rows ROWS.json --labels LABELS.json --out REPORT.md`: refuses unless the labels hash matches the freeze and every label is a bool; prints and writes per-arm counts (arms base, B, C; 10 find samples each) of every label below, with no pass/fail gate and no claim of a rate. Header: `Diagnostic screen, 10 samples per arm. Counts only; proves no general rate.`
LABELS (a human writes them blind from the sheets; define them as constants with a one-line rubric each): `attempted_lift_of_bench` (text has Kristin trying or proposing to lift or move the bench or seat), `completed_lift_of_bench` (text says the lift or move happened), `final_bench_place_changed` (text puts the bench somewhere else), `route_or_face_or_identity_revealed` (reveals the transport route, the photograph's face/contents or who the follower is), `premature_brandon_naming` (the narrator names or has Brandon present before the player earned him), `extra_object_invented` (any object beyond the three declared clues), `meta_narration` (the narrator talks about the story, the game or what will be revealed), `unsolicited_brandon_dialogue` (Brandon speaks, warns or recalls speech although Kristin did not address him), `conveys_three_objects_and_keeping` (the narrator text PLUS appended engine text together show all three declared objects and Kristin keeping them).

TESTS (hermetic): capture builds the arm payloads without HTTP; validate passes on the real package and fails when you tamper a temp copy (for example a second line changed in B, or a clue name injected into an opening payload); C removal fails loudly on zero or two matching lines; dry-run caps; run stops on 429 without replacing a sample and refuses an existing output file and missing env; sheets hide the arm and the key is a bijection; report refuses a tampered labels hash and computes per-arm counts.
